title: Deploy modware-stock via Pulumi
description:
Create local Pulumi stack and deploy modware-stock to the local k3d cluster.

Setup env:
  PASSPHRASE=$(pass show pulumi/local-passphrase | head -n 1)
  export PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE="$PASSPHRASE"
  export KUBECONFIG=$(k3d kubeconfig write k3d-dev-cluster)

Create stack:
  just local-pulumi new-stack modware-stock local pulumi/local-passphrase

Set config (use set-all pattern — one call instead of N):
  pulumi -C modware-stock config set-all --stack local --path \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.namespace=dev' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.appName=stock' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.port=9345' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.logLevel=debug' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.command=start-server' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.image.name=dictybase/modware-stock' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.image.tag=develop-2985bd5' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.arangodbSecret.name=backend' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.arangodbSecret.userkey=user' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.arangodbSecret.passkey=password'

Deploy:
  just local-pulumi create-resource modware-stock local pulumi/local-passphrase

Note: key names use lowercase 'userkey'/'passkey' (differs from modware-annotation which uses capital K).
close_reason: Deployed modware-stock via Pulumi to k3d. Image ghcr.io/dictybase/modware-stock:92ec242. Fixed arm64 ArangoDB scheduling by destroying and recreating arangodb-single stack so operator initializes member fresh with architecture:arm64.

comments.author: Siddhartha Basu
comments.text:
## Deployment Plan

### Image
- Registry: ghcr.io/dictybase/modware-stock
- Tag: 92ec242
- Full ref: ghcr.io/dictybase/modware-stock:92ec242

### Step 1 — Environment Setup
```bash
PASSPHRASE=$(pass show pulumi/local-passphrase | head -n 1)
export PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE="$PASSPHRASE"
export KUBECONFIG=$(k3d kubeconfig write k3d-dev-cluster)
```

### Step 2 — Create Local Stack
```bash
just local-pulumi new-stack modware-stock local pulumi/local-passphrase
```
This initialises a passphrase-encrypted local stack and creates Pulumi.local.yaml in the modware-stock directory.

### Step 3 — Configure the Stack
Key differences from the issue template:
- image.name changed to ghcr.io/dictybase/modware-stock
- image.tag changed to 92ec242
- arangodbSecret keys use lowercase userkey/passkey (as noted in the issue)

```bash
pulumi -C modware-stock config set-all --stack local --path \
    --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.namespace=dev' \
    --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.appName=stock' \
    --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.port=9345' \
    --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.logLevel=debug' \
    --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.command=start-server' \
    --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.image.name=ghcr.io/dictybase/modware-stock' \
    --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.image.tag=92ec242' \
    --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.arangodbSecret.name=backend' \
    --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.arangodbSecret.userkey=user' \
    --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.arangodbSecret.passkey=password'
```

### Step 4 — Deploy
```bash
just local-pulumi create-resource modware-stock local pulumi/local-passphrase
```

### Expected Kubernetes Resources
The backend.go program creates:
- Deployment: stock-api-server (1 replica, namespace dev)
  - Container image: ghcr.io/dictybase/modware-stock:92ec242
  - Env: ARANGODB_USER and ARANGODB_PASSWORD from secret 'backend'
  - Args: --log-level debug start-server --user $(ARANGODB_USER) --pass $(ARANGODB_PASSWORD) --port 9345
- Service: stock-api (ClusterIP, port 9345, namespace dev)

### Notes
- KUBECONFIG must point to k3d-dev-cluster throughout; do not switch global context
- Pulumi local backend state is stored in pulumi-files/local-state
- The Pulumi.local.yaml will use encryptionsalt (passphrase-based, not GCP KMS like experiments stack)

comments.author: Siddhartha Basu
comments.text:
## Plan: Deploy NATS to Local k3d Cluster

### Approach
Create a local Pulumi stack for the existing `nats/` Pulumi program (Helm-based).
No code changes needed — only stack config and deployment.

### Config (local stack vs experiments)
| Key | Experiments | Local |
|-----|-------------|-------|
| storage.class | dictycr-balanced | local-path |
| storage.size | 20Gi | 1Gi |
| chart.name | nats | nats |
| chart.version | 1.2.4 | 1.2.4 |
| image.tag | 2.10.20-alpine | 2.10.20-alpine |
| namespace | dev | dev |

### Steps
1. Create local stack: `just local-pulumi new-stack nats local pulumi/local-passphrase`
2. Set config:
```
pulumi -C nats config set-all --stack local --path \
    --plaintext 'nats:properties.namespace=dev' \
    --plaintext 'nats:properties.chart.name=nats' \
    --plaintext 'nats:properties.chart.repository=https://nats-io.github.io/k8s/helm/charts' \
    --plaintext 'nats:properties.chart.version=1.2.4' \
    --plaintext 'nats:properties.image.tag=2.10.20-alpine' \
    --plaintext 'nats:properties.storage.class=local-path' \
    --plaintext 'nats:properties.storage.size=1Gi'
```
3. Deploy: `just local-pulumi create-resource nats local pulumi/local-passphrase`

### Verification
```
kubectl -n dev get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=nats
kubectl -n dev get svc nats
```
Expected: pod Running, service nats on port 4222.

title: Restore arangodump databases into ArangoDB
description:
Port-forward to ArangoDB then run arangorestore to load all databases from scratch/arangodump/ into the local k3d instance.

Steps:
1. kubectl port-forward -n dev service/arangodb-single-diejsnkq 8529:8529
2. ROOT_PASS=$(pass show arangodb/local-root | head -n 1)
3. docker run --rm --net=host -v "${PWD}/scratch/arangodump:/dump" arangodb/arangodb:3.11.6 arangorestore --server.endpoint tcp://127.0.0.1:8529 --server.username root --server.password "$ROOT_PASS" --input-directory /dump --all-databases true --create-database true

Databases to restore: _system, annofeature, annotation, cgm_ddb, chado, content, order, stock
Skip: lost+found (filesystem artifact)

Restore _system first to set up ArangoDB system collections.
close_reason: Databases restored via just arangodb restore-local-arangodb. All 8 DBs present: _system, annofeature, annotation, cgm_ddb, chado, content, order, stock.
